obligation: CERCLA release notice to the National Response Center
trigger: Release of a hazardous substance at or above its reportable quantity in any 24-hour period. Ammonia RQ 100 lb (for 29% solution count the ammonia content, 302.6(b)(1)(i)); sodium hypochlorite RQ 100 lb; sulfuric acid 1,000 lb; hydrochloric acid 5,000 lb
deadline: Immediately, as soon as the person in charge knows of the release
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - regardless of cause (cyber or not)

obligation: EPCRA emergency release notice (immediate)
trigger: Release of an EPCRA extremely hazardous substance or CERCLA hazardous substance at or above its RQ with potential offsite exposure. Ammonia is an extremely hazardous substance (RQ 100 lb)
deadline: Immediately
notify: LEPC community emergency coordinator and the SERC of any state likely to be affected
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - regardless of cause

obligation: EPCRA written follow-up notice
trigger: After an immediate EPCRA notice
deadline: As soon as practicable after the release
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if an immediate notice was made

obligation: Notify emergency responders (RMP non-responding source)
trigger: Any need for emergency response to an accidental release from the ammonia process
deadline: When there is a need for a response; give timely data on the nature of the release
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - plant employees do not respond to releases

obligation: RMP incident investigation
trigger: Incident that resulted in or could reasonably have resulted in a catastrophic release (includes a cyber intrusion that changed ammonia setpoints or alarms)
deadline: Start as promptly as possible, not later than 48 hours after the incident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: RMP five-year accident history correction
trigger: Accidental release from the covered process with deaths, injuries, or significant on-site property damage, or known offsite impacts
deadline: Within six months of the release, or by the next RMP update if earlier
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the 68.42 criteria are met

obligation: RMP public meeting after an accident with offsite impacts
trigger: RMP reportable accident with known offsite impacts (68.42(a))
deadline: Within 90 days of the accident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if offsite impacts occur

obligation: OSHA severe injury and fatality report
trigger: Work-related fatality; in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye
deadline: Fatality within 8 hours; hospitalization, amputation, or eye loss within 24 hours
notify: OSHA Area Office or 1-800-321-6742, or online
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a worker is harmed

obligation: Voluntary cyber incident report
citation: CISA and FBI voluntary reporting; CISA RBPS 8 guidance (C-CHEMICAL-R01, voluntary benchmark)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed intrusion into OT
deadline: No legal deadline; company target within 24 hours of declaration (POL-03)
notify: CISA (online incident reporting form reached from cisa.gov/report) and the FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary - recommended; also a mitigating factor for OFAC

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (employee personal information)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (for example HR or payroll data taken from the business network during the incident)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Affected Florida residents (employees and former employees)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information was accessed; not held in the PCBMS

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - 162 current employees; count former employees whose data was affected

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely at this headcount

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor holding employee personal information (HR and payroll SaaS) has a breach
deadline: Within 10 days after determination (vendor duty)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in the HR vendor contract

obligation: Other states' breach laws
trigger: Affected employees who reside outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of affected employees

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (typically as soon as practicable; call the carrier hotline before hiring vendors)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: CFATS significant security incident report (RBPS 15)
trigger: Significant security incident at a covered facility
deadline: Not enforceable
applies_at_this_tier: No - CFATS authority expired 2023-07-28 and not reauthorized as of 2026-09-26; report voluntarily to CISA instead

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief; 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - no final rule as of 2026-09-26; as proposed the company is under the SBA size criterion and the CFATS sector criterion is moot

obligation: Reporting of actual or threatened cyber incidents at MTSA facilities / OCS facilities / vessels
trigger: Cyber incident at an MTSA-regulated facility
deadline: Immediately (6.16-1); without delay to the National Response Center
notify: FBI, CISA, and the Coast Guard Captain of the Port; or National Response Center
applies_at_this_tier: No - inland plant with no marine transfer; not a 33 CFR Part 105 facility

obligation: Covered telecommunications / Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
